description.short: Gigrin Farm is the UK's official Red Kite Feeding Centre, where up to 600 wild red kites gather daily for a spectacular aerial display. Located half a mile from Rhayader in Mid Wales, the farm has been feeding red kites every single day since 1992/93, playing a central role in saving the species from extinction in the UK.
description.full:
Gigrin Farm is a 200-acre family-run farm in the heart of Mid Wales, now world-famous as the UK's official Red Kite Feeding Centre. Located just half a mile from the market town of Rhayader, overlooking both the Wye and Elan Valleys, the farm attracts between 300 and 600 wild Red Kites every day for a feeding spectacle that has continued unbroken since 1992/93.

The feeding station was established at the request of the RSPB when Red Kites faced extinction across the UK. Founder Eithel Powell began supplementary feeding daily, and over three decades, the kite population recovered so successfully that they are no longer endangered. Gigrin Farm is widely recognised as one of conservation's greatest success stories and remains an official RSPB feeding centre to this day.

Visitors can watch from five large hides — three wheelchair accessible — or book into specialist photographic hides positioned just metres from the feeding ground. The 200 acres include a farm trail through diverse grassland and woodland, a wetland area, an interpretive centre with watercolour artworks and multimedia exhibits on local raptors, live badger CCTV footage, and a touch-screen database on regional wildlife.

Farm facilities include a coffee shop serving homemade cakes, a gift shop, and a picnic area. The farm is notably home to several rare leucistic (white) Red Kites — among approximately ten known in the world, with three regularly visiting Gigrin. The farm is currently managed by Dominique Powell and Thomas Brickwood, continuing the family legacy.
